section: Hong Kong: The National Security Law
claim: At eleven o'clock on the night of June 30, 2020, the Law of the People's Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region took effect.
source: [1] Law of the People's Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, promulgated and effective June 30, 2020, at 11:00 p.m. local time. **Verified:** the full text was published only at the moment of commencement, and Hong Kong's Legislative Council never voted on it.

claim: Hong Kong is a Chinese city of roughly seven and a half million people, handed from British administration to the People's Republic in 1997 under a written treaty, the Sino-British Joint Declaration of 1984, registered with the United Nations, that guaranteed its freedoms, its separate legal system, and its way of life for fifty years, until 2047, under the formula known as One Country, Two Systems.
source: [2] Sino-British Joint Declaration, signed December 19, 1984, registered with the United Nations Treaty Series. Basic Law of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, effective July 1, 1997.

section: Legal: The Instrument That Did the Work
claim: In 2024 a local ordinance under Article 23 finally added a further tier of offenses.
source: [3] Safeguarding National Security Ordinance (Article 23 legislation), enacted March 2024.

claim: The arrest of Jimmy Lai on August 10, 2020, was conducted by some two hundred officers, filmed and publicized, the publisher walked through his own newsroom in front of cameras.
source: [6] Arrest of Jimmy Lai, August 10, 2020. Officer numbers from contemporaneous reporting and Hong Kong Police Force statements. Subsequent prosecutions of Lai and the forty-seven organizers are matters of court record.

section: Cultural: Erasing the Memory of Resistance
claim: The annual June 4 vigil for the victims of Tiananmen, held in Hong Kong for thirty years, the only place on Chinese soil where it was possible, was prohibited, its organizing alliance disbanded, and its small museum closed.
source: [7] Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic Democratic Movements of China disbanded September 2021; June 4th Museum closed 2021. Court proceedings on the protest anthem, 2023–2024.

claim: In the **Association** domain, the 2021 electoral overhaul that reserved office for vetted patriots captured the local institutions through which the operation was administered.
source: [8] NPC Standing Committee decision on improving the electoral system of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, March 2021.

claim: The law claimed worldwide jurisdiction under Article 38, and the authorities later posted bounties of roughly a million Hong Kong dollars on named activists abroad and issued warrants for citizens of other countries, extending the law's reach to the diaspora so there was no safe distance.
source: [9] National Security Law, Article 38, claiming jurisdiction over offenses committed outside Hong Kong by non-residents. HK$1 million bounties announced by the Hong Kong Police Force in July and December 2023.
